evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/marketplace.rs:922-951 — award_quote (wired POST /api/v1/marketplace/rfqs/{id}/award at marketplace.rs:246) authorizes ONLY the parent RFQ: load_rfq_for_org(&state, user.user_id, id) verifies the path {id} RFQ belongs to the caller's org. It then calls marketplace_repo.award_rfq(id, data.quote_id) where data.quote_id comes straight from the request body (AwardQuoteRequest.quote_id: Uuid, marketplace.rs:93) and is NEVER validated to belong to this RFQ or to the caller's org.

backend/crates/db/src/repositories/marketplace.rs:781-835 — award_rfq(id, quote_id) resolves the quote via find_quote_by_id(quote_id) (by id alone, no rfq_id/org predicate) to derive provider_id, then `UPDATE rfqs SET status='awarded', awarded_to=$2, awarded_quote_id=$3 WHERE id=$1` — the only constraint is rfqs.id=$1; there is no `AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM provider_quotes WHERE id=quote_id AND rfq_id=id)` guard. A manager who owns RFQ-A can award it to a quote_id that belongs to a DIFFERENT RFQ (potentially another tenant's), corrupting RFQ-A.awarded_quote_id/awarded_to with an unrelated provider that never quoted RFQ-A.

backend/crates/db/src/repositories/marketplace.rs:808-817 — the same call then runs `UPDATE provider_quotes SET status='accepted', updated_at=NOW() WHERE id=$1` bound to the client quote_id: a cross-RFQ (and cross-tenant) state write that flips an unrelated provider's quote to 'accepted'. The sibling reject step (marketplace.rs:820-831) correctly scopes `WHERE rfq_id=$1 AND id!=$2`, highlighting that the accept step's missing rfq_id constraint is an in-file inconsistency, not an intentional design.

Same IDOR class as the 2026-07-22 ai/ocr submit_correction finding: parent-org membership is checked, but a client-supplied foreign id (quote_id) is persisted/actioned without validating it belongs to the authorized parent. Fix: resolve the quote inside award_rfq (or in the handler) and reject unless quote.rfq_id == id, e.g. add `AND rfq_id = $1` to the find and to both provider_quotes updates.

Secondary correctness defect in the same method: award_rfq has no status guard (contrast cancel_rfq at marketplace.rs:837 which uses `WHERE id=$1 AND status NOT IN ('awarded','cancelled')`), so an already-awarded or cancelled RFQ can be re-awarded, re-flipping quote statuses each call.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/layout/admin.rs:15-20 (bad_request helper) returns StatusCode::UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY (422), and every admin handler funnels its DB failures through it: list_screens (:41,:45), get_config (:69,:74,:84,:88), put_draft (:118,:122), put_rails (:149,:153), list_manifests (:176,:180), put_manifest (:216,:220), publish (:247,:253,:271,:294), rollback (:319), kill (:356,:360), preview_resolve (:401,:407,:420), unkill (:449,:453). This maps infrastructure/connection failures (acquire_public() errors and sqlx query errors) to a client-side 4xx meaning 'your input is unprocessable'. Two concrete consequences: (1) a Postgres outage or pool exhaustion on any layout-admin endpoint surfaces as 422, which 5xx-based alerting/SLO monitors do not fire on -> DB outages are silently swallowed on this path; (2) API clients are told their well-formed request was rejected as invalid. Confirmed to be an oversight, not intent: the two SIBLING handler files in the same module handle identical DB errors correctly with StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR -- tenant.rs:28-35,:40-47,:51-58,:68-75,:206-213 and resolved.rs:35-40 (err500) at :70,:76,:80,:86,:95,:98,:103,:111. admin.rs reused its validation-error closure for infra errors too. Fix: give admin.rs a distinct err500 path (mirroring resolved.rs's err500 closure) for acquire_public()/repo DB errors, reserving bad_request (422) for the genuine parse/validation branches.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/layout/admin.rs:46,:123,:154,:181,:221,:296 and tenant.rs:214 -- successful responses are built with serde_json::to_value(row).unwrap_or_default(). On a serialization failure the .unwrap_or_default() yields serde_json::Value::Null, so the handler returns 200 OK with a body of literal null instead of a 500. A caller (ppt-web layout admin UI) that just performed a publish/rollback/put-draft/put-rails/put-manifest would receive a success status with no payload and no error signal, masking a genuine serialization bug as a successful empty write. Low severity because the row types reliably serialize today, but the pattern is a latent silent-failure across 7 write/read sites. Fix: map the serialization error to a 500 path rather than defaulting to Null (Json(serde_json::to_value(row).map_err(err500)?)).
